passages.text: You should read the following discussion in conjunction with our audited consolidated financial statements, including the notes thereto, which are included elsewhere in this Form 10-K. Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations contains statements that are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risk, uncertainties, and other factors and speak only as of the filing date. Actual results could differ materially because of the factors discussed in "Risk Factors" and elsewhere in this Form 10-K. Executive Overview This executive overview presents summarized information regarding our business and operating trends only. For further details, please read "Management's Discussion and Analysis of Financial Condition and Results of Operations" in its entirety. onsemi Results Our revenue for the year ended December 31, 2025 was $5,995.4 million, representing a decrease of 15.3% from $7,082.3 million for the year ended December 31, 2024. During 2025, we reported net income attributable to onsemi of $121.0 million compared to $1,572.8 million in 2024. Our operating income totaled $84.2 million during 2025 compared to $1,767.7 million during 2024. Our gross margin decreased by approximately 1,230 basis points to 33.1% in 2025 from 45.4% in 2024. Our operating results were significantly impacted by restructuring, asset impairment and other charges resulting from our 2025 Manufacturing Realignment Program. See Note 7: ''Restructuring, Asset Impairments and Other, net'' for additional information. We also continued to experience decreased demand in our automotive and industrial end-markets resulting in lower sales volumes and the corresponding underutilization of our manufacturing facilities. See discussion under "Results of Operations" for the reasons for the fluctuations year-over-year. Business and Macroeconomic Environment The semiconductor industry has traditionally been highly cyclical, and has often experienced significant downturns in connection with, or in anticipation of, declines in general economic conditions. During 2025, the semiconductor industry continued to experience a softening demand and uncertainty due to macroeconomic factors and the geopolitical environment. In this environment, we have focused on operational excellence and cash flow generation. Given the conditions, we are actively managing and have taken corrective actions in our manufacturing capacity and spending to align with the forecasted demand. We intend to continue these actions during 2026. We continue to implement cost-saving initiatives to be able to align our overall cost structure, capital investments and other expenditures with our expected revenue, spending and capacity levels to help offset softening demand and increased manufacturing and operating costs. We have taken, and continue to take actions, including but not limited to, exiting product lines that do not enhance gross margin or satisfy strategic objectives. We made meaningful progress in aligning internal manufacturing capacity and resources to external demand. See Note 7: ''Restructuring, Asset Impairment

Trends, Risks and Uncertainties Related to Our Business The manufacturing and other operations required to produce our products are highly dependent on the efficient operation of numerous processes, including processes contingent upon third-party component manufacturers and other service providers, and any disruption in these processes could have a material adverse effect on our business and results of operations. Our manufacturing network includes multiple owned and third-party facilities, which may each produce one or more components necessary for the assembly of a single product. credit_strengths.text: Operating cash flow comfortably exceeds share repurchases, so internal generation funds the buyback programme without incremental borrowing. Free cash flow also covers buybacks, leaving a modest surplus after distributions. This self-funding capacity is the core support for the credit, though it rests on cyclical semiconductor demand.

Liquidity is a clear strength: the current ratio sits well above the sector median and above unity, with cash covering a large share of gross debt. Net leverage on a cash-and-investments basis is modest and remains below the next risk-band boundary, giving meaningful headroom against an earnings downturn.

key_risks.text: The debt note shows a large zero-coupon maturity due in year two and a further note due in year three, with nothing due in the next twelve months. Refinancing is therefore concentrated in the medium term and must be met from cash or new issuance in a weaker operating climate.

Risk factors flag the interdependence of the manufacturing network, where a disruption at a single owned or third-party facility can disproportionately impair output across many products. Combined with the disclosed automotive and industrial demand weakness, this concentrates operational and cyclical risk in a capital-intensive footprint.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage has fallen sharply year on year and sits far below the sector median, reflecting the collapse in operating income rather than higher borrowing. Coverage remains above unity, but the thin margin means earnings volatility, not the debt stack, now drives servicing headroom.

Cash flow coverage of debt is strong in absolute terms and improved year on year, though it trails the sector median. Free cash flow to debt also improved and is close to the peer median, indicating that cash generation, rather than EBITDA, is the more reliable servicing anchor for this issuer.

overall_credit_view.text: Gross leverage rose sharply year on year and stands well above the sector median, while the operating margin collapsed to a fraction of prior-year and peer levels on restructuring and underutilization charges. The indicative financial risk profile remains minimal on a net-debt basis, but the earnings trend is the key watch item.

Our judgement is that the issuer retains solid investment-grade-like capacity: cash and free cash flow comfortably address near-term maturities, and buybacks are funded internally. The credit is nonetheless exposed to a cyclical trough, so we would monitor restructuring execution and demand recovery before viewing leverage improvement as durable.

credit_strengths.text: 營運現金流穩健地超過股份回購金額，因此內部產生的資金足以支持回購計劃，而無需新增借貸。自由現金流亦足以覆蓋回購，於分派後仍留有溫和盈餘。此自我融資能力是該信貸的核心支撐，惟其依賴週期性的半導體需求。
流動性為明顯優勢：流動比率遠高於行業中位數且高於一，現金覆蓋總債務的相當大比例。以現金及投資計算的淨槓桿溫和，並維持於下一個風險區間界線之下，對盈利下滑提供有意義的緩衝空間。

key_risks.text: 債務附註顯示一筆於第二年到期的大額零息債務，以及另一筆於第三年到期的票據，未來十二個月內並無到期債務。因此再融資集中於中期，並須在較疲弱的經營環境下以現金或新發行滿足。
風險因素指出製造網絡的相互依存性，單一自有或第三方設施的中斷可對眾多產品的產出造成不成比例的損害。結合已披露的汽車及工業需求疲弱，此舉將營運及週期性風險集中於資本密集的資產基礎。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率按年大幅下降，並遠低於行業中位數，反映經營收入崩跌而非借貸增加。覆蓋率仍高於一，但利潤緩衝薄弱意味著盈利波動、而非債務結構，現時主導償債緩衝空間。
債務的現金流覆蓋率絕對值強勁並按年改善，惟落後於行業中位數。自由現金流對債務比率亦有所改善並接近同業中位數，顯示現金產生、而非 EBITDA，為此發行人更可靠的償債錨點。

overall_credit_view.text: 總槓桿按年大幅上升，並遠高於行業中位數，而經營利潤率因重組及產能利用率不足費用而崩跌至去年及同業水平的一小部分。以淨債務計算的指示性財務風險狀況仍為極低，惟盈利趨勢為關鍵觀察項目。
我們的判斷是發行人仍保有穩健的類投資級能力：現金及自由現金流穩健地應對近期到期債務，而回購由內部資金支持。惟該信貸仍暴露於週期性低谷，因此我們會監察重組執行及需求復甦，方視槓桿改善為持久。
